children: ICICI Bank garnered $17.88 billion (Rs 1.70 lakh crore) under the foreign currency non-resident bank deposit scheme, making the private lender among the first to reveal its gross FCNR-B mobilisation.
Standby letters of credit (SBLC) issued to other banks against such deposits total $3.63 billion, India’s second-largest private lender said in an exchange filing.
The bank has issued in aggregate $3.55 billion of dollar-denominated bonds during July-August period.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)’s special concessional window for FCNR-B deposits closed to an early end on August 31.
The central bank caught the market by surprise in mid-August by bringing forward the deadline for FCNR-B deposits, citing an "encouraging response".
Other leading private lenders such as HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank are yet to share their final FCNR-B deposit figures.

According to the latest RBI data, FCNR-B deposits garnered just over $65 billion, while overall inflows, including external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), crossed $72 billion as of August 21.

To shore up capital inflows, the RBI introduced a string of measures in early June, including hedging cost support for three- and five-year FCNR-B deposits, alongside a concessional swap window for external commercial borrowings (ECBs) by public sector entities.
Moneycontrol has reported that market participants are expecting at least $75 billion to come in via FCNR-B deposits.
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank offered at least 9x leverage on these deposits and HSBC Bank up to 19x.

To be sure, HSBC was among the top lenders said to have garnered the maximum flows, according to recent parliamentary data from July 30, securing inflows of nearly $6 billion. This was closely followed by State Bank of India with roughly $4 billion.

title: ICICI Bank garners $17.88 billion in FCNR-B deposits
